title: Mass versus weight
canonical_question: What is the difference between mass and weight?
summary: Mass measures how much matter is in a body and how strongly it resists acceleration; it is the same everywhere.
Mass is measured in kilograms, a measure of inertia, while weight is a force measured in newtons.

reuse.rationale: Authored fixture node for the E05 registry.

sections.heading: Two different quantities
sections.body_md: Mass measures how much matter is in a body and how strongly it resists acceleration; it is the same everywhere. Weight is the gravitational force pulling on that mass, so it changes with location. On the Moon your mass is unchanged but your weight is about a sixth of its Earth value.

sections.heading: Units give it away
sections.body_md: Mass is measured in kilograms, a measure of inertia, while weight is a force measured in newtons. Weight equals mass times the local gravitational field strength, so w = mg. Confusing the two is why people wrongly think objects "lose mass" in space.

key_points: Mass is amount of matter and inertia, in kilograms.
Weight is a gravitational force, in newtons.
w = mg links them through local gravity.
core.bridge_to_parent: It sharpens the meaning of mass used in F = ma.
